items.title: Jimmy Owens — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: That’s not how Billy Eckstine dealt with it. That’s not how Charlie Parker dealt with it, or Art Tatum, you know, or Miles Davis. Their performances were so strong...

ctx.x: Let’s talk about your recording career, specifically.

Well, after Donald Byrd and that session when I didn’t solo on anything, I worked with Mingus at Monterey and I soloed. That particular band, when we went to Los Angeles and recorded that unknown record, I had solos and I was kind of the band director. I would direct all of the stuff with my horn when I play. There were a lot of things that Mingus wrote that had to be conducted for everyone. It was wonderful working with Julius Watkins, he was a beautiful man and a wonderful musician. You know, Hobard Dotson was…
the—thousands of recordings, may I say?
